review_locator: PMCID:PMC109195, ErbB Tyrosine Kinases and the Two Neuregulin Families Constitute a Ligand-Receptor Network; PMCID:PMC2682371, Neuregulin 1 in neural development, synaptic plasticity and schizophrenia
primary_title: ErbB tyrosine kinases and the two neuregulin families constitute a ligand-receptor network; Binding specificities and affinities of EGF domains for ErbB receptors; Ligands for ErbB-family receptors encoded by a neuregulin-like gene
decision_basis: The review identifies NRG2 as an ErbB3/ErbB4 ligand; primary defined-receptor cell systems show NRG2-beta binding to and activation of ErbB3-containing receptor combinations, with ligand-displacement and phosphorylation/proliferation readouts.
limitations_preserved: Preserve the NRG2-beta isoform and ErbB3-containing receptor-combination context; the primary system is engineered and does not establish a native neural or SCI receiver branch.

review_locator: PMCID:PMC109195, ErbB Tyrosine Kinases and the Two Neuregulin Families Constitute a Ligand-Receptor Network; PMCID:PMC2682371, Neuregulin 1 in neural development, synaptic plasticity and schizophrenia
primary_title: ErbB tyrosine kinases and the two neuregulin families constitute a ligand-receptor network; Binding specificities and affinities of EGF domains for ErbB receptors; Ligands for ErbB-family receptors encoded by a neuregulin-like gene
decision_basis: The review identifies NRG2 as an ErbB4 ligand; primary receptor-defined systems show NRG2-beta binding to and activating ErbB4-containing combinations, with displacement, receptor phosphorylation and IL-3-independent/proliferative readouts.
limitations_preserved: Preserve the NRG2-beta isoform and ErbB4-containing receptor-combination context; do not infer a unique ErbB4 homodimer or native CNS/SCI branch from engineered-cell assays.

review_locator: PMCID:PMC109195, ErbB Tyrosine Kinases and the Two Neuregulin Families Constitute a Ligand-Receptor Network; PMID:24991953, Neuregulin-ERBB signaling in the nervous system and neuropsychiatric diseases
primary_title: Neuregulin-3: a novel neural tissue-enriched protein that binds and activates ErbB4
decision_basis: The reviews identify NRG3 as a neural-enriched ErbB4 ligand; the cited primary study demonstrates NRG3 EGF-like-domain binding to ErbB4 extracellular domain and cell-surface ErbB4, together with ErbB4 tyrosine phosphorylation.
limitations_preserved: Promote only NRG3-ErbB4 binding/activation; preserve neural-enriched ligand context and do not infer an ErbB2-containing complex or SCI function.

review_locator: PMCID:PMC3695728, Exploring mechanisms of FGF signalling through the lens of structural biology; PMCID:PMC2080618, Receptor specificity of the fibroblast growth factor family
primary_title: Structural basis by which alternative splicing modulates the organizer activity of FGF8 in the brain
decision_basis: The reviews identify the FGF8b-FGFR2c structural pair; the cited primary study resolves the extracellular complex, maps the splice-specific interface by SPR/mutagenesis, and links receptor-binding differences to developmental activity.
limitations_preserved: Preserve the FGF8b isoform and FGFR2c splice variant; promote the exact extracellular binding/assembly and bounded developmental function, without generic FGFR2 or SCI extrapolation.

review_locator: PMCID:PMC3695728, Exploring mechanisms of FGF signalling through the lens of structural biology; PMCID:PMC2080618, Receptor specificity of the fibroblast growth factor family
primary_title: Structural basis by which alternative splicing confers specificity in fibroblast growth factor receptors
decision_basis: The reviews identify FGF10-FGFR2b as a splice-specific receptor pair; the cited primary study resolves the ligand-binding portion of FGFR2b bound to FGF10 and validates interface contacts by structure-based mutagenesis and biological activity assays.
limitations_preserved: Preserve the FGFR2b splice isoform and heparan-sulfate/receptor-domain context; promote exact structural binding/assembly and bounded activity only, not the broad FGF10-FGFR2 SCI pathway row.

review_locator: PMCID:PMC3777820, Eph/ephrin recognition and signaling review; PMCID:PMC3327877, Eph/ephrin cell-cell signaling review
primary_title: Crystal structure of the ephrin-B1 ectodomain: implications for receptor recognition and signaling; Juxtamembrane tyrosine residues couple the Eph family receptor EphB2/Nuk to specific SH2 domain proteins in neuronal cells
decision_basis: The reviews identify ephrin-B1 as an EphB2 ligand; primary structural/biophysical work characterizes ephrin-B1 receptor-binding preference, while EphB2-expressing neuronal cells show ephrin-B1-induced receptor phosphorylation and downstream SH2-adaptor signaling.
limitations_preserved: Preserve membrane/clustered ephrin-B1 and EphB2 bidirectional-signaling topology; the neuronal assay supports EphB2 forward relay, not an autonomous ephrin-B1 reverse pathway or SCI-specific claim.
